title: Lazur vs Apple Dictation on Mac in 2026: when free built-in dictation is enough
metaTitle: Lazur vs Apple Dictation: which one fits your Mac
description: Lazur vs Apple Dictation on Mac: Apple Dictation is free and built in, while Lazur adds a screen-aware voice assistant for $18/month after a trial.
intro: Apple Dictation is free and built into macOS. It types what you say into text fields, and you install nothing. Lazur Pro costs $18/month after a 3-day trial. Lazur dictates too, but it also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and talks back.
tldr: Apple Dictation types what you say. It costs nothing and ships with macOS.
Lazur dictates too, but it also answers questions about your screen and points at buttons.
Pick Apple Dictation if typing by voice is the whole job.
Pick Lazur if you often get stuck in apps. Pro is $18/month after a 3-day trial.

blocks.text: Apple Dictation vs Lazur in one sentence

Apple Dictation turns your speech into text at the cursor, and that is where it stops. Lazur turns speech into text too, but it also answers questions about what is on your screen, points at things and guides you through apps. If you only need to type by voice, the two overlap. If you need help with the app in front of you, they do not.
What Apple Dictation does on a Mac

Apple Dictation is the speech input built into macOS. Apple's current Mac help guide covers macOS 27 Golden Gate. You do not install an app, and you do not sign up for an account. The Apple pages checked for this comparison list no price for Dictation. Voibe, a paid dictation app, and Zapier both describe it as included with macOS at no extra cost. Those are reviewer opinions, not Apple's claims.

Apple's guide says you can dictate text of any length without a timeout. It also says Dictation stops after 30 seconds without speech. Punctuation is automatic, and you can turn it off. That matters if you want plain words with no commas or full stops added for you.
How to turn on Apple Dictation on Mac

items: Choose Apple menu > System Settings > Keyboard.
Turn on Dictation. Pick the shortcut you want, or keep the default.
Click into a text field, such as a note in Notes or a reply in Mail.
Press the Microphone key, your shortcut, or choose Edit > Start Dictation.
Speak. Stop when you finish, or let the 30-second silence timeout stop it.

blocks.text: If nothing happens, click into a text field first. Dictation types into the field that has the cursor. That one habit fixes most first-time confusion.

The Apple Intelligence model that fixes spelling, punctuation and capitalization is English only. Apple's guide says it needs a Mac with M3 or later and at least 12GB of unified memory. If your Mac does not meet that, the model is not available to you.
Free dictation on Mac: what it costs and what could change

Apple's pages do not list a price for Dictation. Apple's macOS page does not state one, and its Mac help guide does not either. A footnote in the guide covers server-side Apple Intelligence features, such as Siri AI and Image Playground. It says expanded access to those will be available for a fee in the future. Dictation is not named in that footnote.
Apple could change its terms later. Check that footnote again before you plan a budget around Dictation. For now, the wording on Apple's pages keeps Dictation out of that fee line.
Where Lazur is a good Apple Dictation alternative

Lazur lives in the notch at the top of your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option plus Command, to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app.

Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. You do the clicks. Lazur circles the button and waits for you.

Lazur also handles everyday work by voice. That covers timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts. Background research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension, and comes back with a summary and a report.
Dictation quality: punctuation, names and your own words

Apple Dictation adds punctuation automatically. The Apple Intelligence model also handles spelling and capitalization, within the hardware limits above. Voibe says Apple Dictation has no custom vocabulary, so names, jargon and technical terms can come out wrong. That is a paid competitor's opinion. Test it with your own names before you rely on it.

Lazur's dictation adds a personal dictionary, snippets and clipboard slots. A personal dictionary teaches the app your names once. Snippets expand a short phrase into a longer block, such as an address you type often. Clipboard slots hold text you want to paste later.
Worked example: one client email, two apps
Take one reply to a client. You dictate it in Mail with Apple Dictation. The sentences come out with punctuation, but the client's surname turns into a common word. You fix it by hand, then move on.

Next, add the surname to Lazur's personal dictionary and dictate the same reply. Hold fn, speak, and check the result. The name has a better chance to come out right. You still read the reply before you send it.
The difference is not the typing. It is the fix you make after the typing. If you rarely fix names, Apple Dictation is enough. If you fix names every day, a personal dictionary is worth testing.
Where Apple Dictation is the better pick

items: You want dictation and nothing else, at no cost.
Your notes, messages and drafts live in Apple apps, and you type in them all day.
You do not want another app running in the notch or in the background.
Your dictation sessions are short, so the 30-second silence stop rarely gets in the way.
You want general text processed on your device on a supported Mac, under Apple's current guide.

blocks.text: Zapier calls Apple Dictation very fast. It also says the tool is limited for professional dictation workflows. Both lines are opinions, not measured results. No independent accuracy test turned up for Apple Dictation, so run your own check before you trust it with contracts or clinical notes.
Voibe gives Apple Dictation 6.5/10 and calls it “An excellent free baseline with a clear ceiling.” Voibe sells a paid dictation app and discloses that on its page. Read the score as one opinion.
Where Lazur is the better pick

items: You get stuck in apps and want something to point at the button.
You want to ask what a menu item does, or what is on screen, without leaving the app.
You want timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events and music by voice too.
You want background research that comes back with a summary and a report.
You want memory of what you asked and did, kept on your Mac.

blocks.text: Lazur fits when the problem is not typing. The problem is finding where a setting lives. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask where it is, and Lazur circles it. Then you click. Apple Dictation is not built for that job.
What Lazur costs compared with free Apple Dictation

Lazur offers a 3-day Pro trial. The trial starts when you first open the app, and no credit card is needed. After that, Pro costs $18/month, or $15/month billed annually, and includes 250 AI actions. Power costs $120/month, or $96/month billed annually, and includes 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

Apple Dictation has no price on Apple's pages, and reviewers describe it as included with macOS. If you dictate all day and never ask for help, the Pro price buys you dictation you could get for free. If you want the screen help too, the price is what that help costs.
Privacy: what Apple does with your voice

Apple's current guide says you can check Keyboard settings to see whether general text Dictation is processed on your device and not sent to Siri servers. The guide says that covers general text dictation. It does not cover dictation in a search box.

Audio storage is opt-in. If you click Share Audio Recordings, Apple may store audio of your Siri and Dictation interactions from your Mac, and Apple may review a sample. You can change that under Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.
Apple's legal page says stored audio is not associated with your Apple Account. Only Apple employees under strict confidentiality can access it. The data may be retained for up to two years.

Apple's macOS 14 guide says something different for some Macs. On an Intel-based Mac, or in a language without on-device dictation, your dictated utterances are sent to Apple. The current guide does not mention Intel Macs. If you use an Intel Mac, check the guide for your macOS version before you rely on on-device processing.

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked and did stays on your Mac.

Lazur's facts say audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer. They do not say where dictated text is processed. Check both sets of privacy wording before you dictate client or medical text.
Mistakes people make with either app

items: Expecting Apple Dictation to see your screen. It types. It does not answer questions about what is on screen.
Losing a thought to the 30-second silence stop. Speak in shorter bursts, then continue after the stop.
Trusting the first draft. Read names, numbers and addresses before you send.
Forgetting that you do the clicks. Lazur circles the button or guides you one click at a time, and you press it.
Using the same shortcut in both apps. Change one in its settings if the keys overlap.
Testing with one short sentence. Use a full paragraph from your real work instead.

blocks.text: Another common slip is turning off automatic punctuation without a clear reason, then fixing commas by hand all day. Leave it on unless you have a real need to turn it off.
How to test both on your own text

items: Pick a paragraph you wrote last week. Include two names and one date.
Open Notes. Dictate the paragraph with Apple Dictation, then count the fixes you make.
Clear the note. Dictate the same paragraph with Lazur, holding fn.
Compare the fixes, the time you spent and any words you had to say again.
Keep the app that needed fewer fixes for that kind of text, and keep the other for its strengths.

blocks.text: Want a number for your own speed first? Run the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test). It shows how fast you speak compared with how fast you type, which tells you how much dictation could save you.
If you want a second check on the text itself, use the [dictation accuracy checker](/tools/dictation-accuracy-checker) on the same paragraph from each app.
Who should pick which

Pick Apple Dictation if typing by voice is all you need and you want to spend nothing. It is built in, and it works wherever your cursor is. Pick Lazur if you want a voice assistant that sees your screen, guides you through apps and dictates in the same place.

You can run both. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask. Apple Dictation starts from the Microphone key or its own shortcut. If the keys overlap, pick different ones so one app does not take the other's keypress.
Want to see the other options first? Read [Apple Dictation alternatives](/alternatives/apple-dictation), which compares price, privacy and strengths for each app.
What survey data says about voice use and AI

Menlo Ventures, citing a Morning Consult survey of 5,067 U.S. adults in July 2026, reports that 46% speak to AI at least some of the time. Among AI users, 19% say voice is their main way of interacting with AI.
That survey measures voice use with AI, not dictation into text fields. It does not tell you how many people use Apple Dictation or Lazur. Use it as context, not as a verdict.
What to do next

Turn on Apple Dictation first. It takes moments, and it costs nothing. Run the test above with one real paragraph. If the fixes annoy you, the [download page](/download) has the Mac app, and the 3-day Pro trial needs no credit card. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) before you choose a paid plan.

faq.question: Is Lazur a good Apple Dictation alternative?
faq.answer: If you want more than dictation, yes. Lazur dictates in any Mac app with hold fn, and it also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you one click at a time. If you only dictate, Apple Dictation covers that for no cost.

faq.question: Is Apple Dictation free on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's pages I checked list no price for Dictation. Zapier and Voibe describe it as included with macOS at no extra cost. Apple's fee footnote names Siri AI and Image Playground, and it does not name Dictation.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and Apple Dictation together?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur dictates with hold fn and asks with hold ⌥ ⌘. Apple Dictation starts with the Microphone key or its own shortcut, so change one if the keys overlap.

faq.question: How do I turn on Apple Dictation on Mac?
faq.answer: Choose Apple menu > System Settings > Keyboard, then turn on Dictation. Start it with the Microphone key, your shortcut, or Edit > Start Dictation. Click into a text field first, because Dictation types into the field with the cursor.

faq.question: Does Apple Dictation send my voice to Apple?
faq.answer: Apple's current guide says general text dictation is processed on your device and not sent to Siri servers. Search-box dictation is not covered by that line. Apple's older macOS 14 guide says Intel Macs send dictated utterances to Apple, so check your own Mac.

faq.question: Does Apple Dictation stop when I pause?
faq.answer: It stops after 30 seconds without speech, according to Apple's guide. Apple says you can dictate text of any length without a timeout. A pause longer than 30 seconds ends the session, so speak in shorter bursts if you pause often.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur runs on macOS on Apple silicon and on Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available yet.

faq.question: How long is the Lazur trial?
faq.answer: Lazur offers a 3-day Pro trial. It starts when you first open the app, and no credit card is needed. After the trial, Pro costs $18/month, or $15/month billed annually.

verdict: Pick Apple Dictation if typing by voice is all you need and you want to spend nothing. Pick Lazur if you want dictation plus help with what is on your screen, from answers to pointing at the button you need. Lazur Pro costs $18/month after a 3-day trial, and dictation is unlimited on both of its plans.
